articles.title: First teaser for Apple TV's Neuromancer debuts at SDCC
articles.text:
Apple TV is fast eclipsing HBO as the go-to platform for prestige TV, especially science fiction, with standout fare like Slow Horses, Severance, Foundation, For All Mankind, Murderbot, Silo, Pluribus, and Widow's Bay, among others. Add the upcoming Neuromancer series to that list, an adaption of William Gibson's hugely influential 1984 cyberpunk novel of the same name. The streaming platform released a short teaser during San Diego Comic-Con, and visually it looks fantastic, even based on one minute of footage.

Saturday's various SDCC panels also gave us a teaser for Prime Video's Carrie; trailers for Dark Matter S2 and Matchbox: The Movie; and a bit of Marvel casting news.

Fans of Gibson's book already know the Neuromancer story; we'll have to wait and see how closely the series will adhere to the novel. Per the official logline, the series "follows a damaged, top-rung super-hacker named Case who is thrust into a web of digital espionage with his partner Molly, a razor-girl assassin with mirrored eyes, aiming to pull a heist on a corporate dynasty with untold secrets." Callum Taylor, best known as Theseus Scamander in the Fantastic Beasts franchise, stars as Case, alongside Briana Middleton (The Inheritance) as Molly.

articles.text:

US President Donald Trump has announced a phased tariff framework under which imported generic medicines will continue to attract zero tariffs until August 1, 2028, before facing a 100 per cent tariff for one year and a 200 per cent tariff from August 1, 2029.
The proposal, aimed at encouraging drug manufacturing in the US, has triggered a debate within India's pharmaceutical sector over its long-term implications.

articles.title: Mirabai Chanu wins Indian's 1st gold in CWG
articles.text: India's star weightlifter Mirabai Chanu won women's 48kg title on Sunday, bagging the maiden gold medal for the country in Glasgow Commonwealth Games 2026.The victory marked Chanu's third consecutive Commonwealth Games gold, having also topped the podium in the 2018 and 2022 editions. The Tokyo Olympics silver medallist had earlier won silver at the 2014 Games.Also read: Neeraj Chopra not obsessed with 90m, says titles and consistency matter more&mdash; India_AllSports (@India_AllSports) Chanu also rewrote the record books, setting new Commonwealth and Commonwealth Games records in the snatch with a best lift of 85kg before lifting a Games record 105kg in the clean and jerk for a winning total of 190kg.She earlier opened with a failed attempt at 82kg before successfully clearing the weight on her second lift. Chanu then lifted 85kg on her final attempt to establish the new snatch record.The gold medal adds to Chanu's remarkable Commonwealth Games record, having previously won titles at the 2018 Gold Coast and 2022 Birmingham Games.Earlier in the day, India narrowly missed another gold in weightlifting as Chanambam Rishikanta Singh clinched silver medal in the men's event despite producing a record-equalling effort in the snatch.Rishikanta finished with a combined total of 264kg (121kg snatch and 143kg clean and jerk). He broke the Commonwealth Games snatch record with a personal-best lift of 121kg, although Malaysia's Mohamad Aniq Kasdan matched the mark before producing a Games record total of 273kg (121kg snatch and 152kg clean and jerk) to claim gold.Rishikanta briefly led the competition after successfully opening with 143kg in the clean and jerk, but Kasdan responded with lifts of 145kg and 149kg to regain the advantage. Needing 151kg on his final attempt to reclaim the lead, the Indian completed the clean but failed to lock out the jerk, ending his bid for gold. Kasdan then capped off his campaign with a successful 152kg lift to seal victory, while Kenya's Joshua Mboya claimed bronze with a total of 260kg (115kg snatch and 145kg clean and jerk).Also read: Rishikanta Singh wins silver in men's 60kg weightlifting at Commonwealth GamesGreetings pour in for Mirabai Chanu; Indian fans rejoice    <blockquote class="twitter-tweet" data-media-max-width="560"><p lang="en" dir="ltr"><a href="https://x.com/hashtag/WATCH?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">#WATCH</a> | Glasgow, Scotland: Indian fans in Glasgow celebrate Mirabai Chanu's Gold Medal in the Women's 48kg Weightlifting event at Commonwealth Games 2026.<br/><br/>Nishtha, an Indian fan says, "I can't explain in words. It was such a surreal moment. I had goosebumps. I am so proud of… <a href="https://t.co/UuQiUcL3qI">pic.twitter.com/UuQiUcL3qI</a></p>— ANI (@ANI) <a href="https://x.com/ANI/status/2081401542918476282?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">July 26, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async="" src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script>On Mirabai Chanu's Gold Medal in the 2026 Commonwealth Games, Indian Olympic Association President PT Usha said, "So excited to see Mirabai Chanu lifting the weight and it's a great moment for me and for all Indians that she won the Commonwealth Gold."Speaking to ANI, PT Usha said that Chanu was confident that she was doing much better.Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulated Chanu on her victory, describing it as "another glorious chapter in Indian weightlifting."In a post on X, Modi said Chanu had once again showcased her skills with a stunning performance in the women's 48kg category and hailed her achievement of winning back-to-back Commonwealth Games gold medals. Calling her an inspiration for every Indian, the he wished her success in her future endeavours.&mdash; narendramodi (@narendramodi) Defence Minister Rajnath Singh also congratulated Mirabai Chanu on winning the Gold Medal in Weightlifting at the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games."Her unwavering determination and relentless pursuit of excellence have brought glory to the nation. This remarkable achievement reflects the spirit of perseverance and dedication that continues to inspire millions of young Indians," he said, wishing her continued success and many more laurels in the years to come.Vice President C. P. Radhakrishnan also greeted the weightlifter saying, "Your consistent medal-winning performances for India at the highest level over the years reflect your exceptional dedication, resilience and pursuit of excellence. Your remarkable achievements over the years have made the entire nation proud."(With inputs from ANI)

articles.title: Show HN: I mapped every US golf course
articles.text:
I got tired of Googling basic course info, so I made a free directory of every US course

Google filters for golf course results are terrible so I built a better way to browse courses using OSM as the backbone.... https://golfcoursebrowser.com/

It's a work in progress and mostly US for now, but I want to expand to the rest of North America, the EU, and the rest of the world ASAP.

It's free, no ads, no login, no bs. If you spot anything wrong (bad info, a missing course, wrong scorecard), you can flag it right on the course page. I actually read those and fix them.

Still a lot of missing info, but I'm filling out more and more each day. The goal is the most complete, and current golf course directory in the world, verified and maintained by actual golfers. I think is attainable in the next few months. The base layer is OpenStreetMap, cross-checked against course websites and enriched with scorecards, USGA rating/slope, and public/private status. User corrections from golfers who know their home course have beaten every commercial data source we check against.
